answer: An agent economy can make identity costly by requiring every account to escrow a scarce token in a vault before it can vote, borrow, or earn fees. A random lotus or willow peer then challenges its signed work and checks consistency across repeated interactions; a failed or duplicated identity is slashed and excluded. Creating a Sybil farm therefore requires funding each account and producing sustained, auditable behavior, while one detected link destroys its bond and future access.
